claims.statement: `tst` carries phenomenon time -- when the thing being described happened. Time series, windowing, and joins to other feeds are built on it.

claims.statement: Successive `tst` values are expected at cadence `fixed` with period "PT1S". A cadence is an expectation and not a constraint: a record that departs from it is late, not invalid, and a missing value must not be filled in because the cadence says one was due.
claims.negative: Treating the cadence as a guarantee of completeness or as a validation rule, or interpolating absent values from it.

prose.note: Strongest is the discipline of measuring every interval itself from consecutive `tst` rather than assuming cadence; weakest is the PERCENTILE_CONT analytic used inside a windowed GROUP BY, which the answer itself doubts and which would not run.

annotated.note: Strongest is the peer residual that separates a sick vehicle from a sick corridor; weakest is cadence_ratio, whose count-over-covered-seconds arithmetic reads as a completeness score and is easy to misinterpret.

spec.note: Strongest is the explicitly grounded refusal set and the units-aware choice of `odo` over coordinate geometry; weakest is the WITHIN GROUP spelling of PERCENTILE_CONT, which is not this dialect's syntax.

bare.note: Strongest is the careful identification of the last record carrying a `stop` as the departure proxy; weakest is discarding `dl` and averaging `occu`, which leaves the two headline metrics resting on unit guesses, plus COUNT(DISTINCT) and LAG over an aggregate that likely will not run.
